answer: Proof-of-escrow collateral: an identity joins the attestation pool only by locking one fixed deposit, like a timber merchant's bond posted once before trading. Each deposit is unique and non-transferable, so forging 1,000 identities costs 1,000 full deposits — the attacker's capital scales linearly with the fraud. An honest agent locks once and reuses the stake forever. Slashing burns the bond of any identity caught duplicating work, so the attacker's plume of fakes collapses the moment peers check the ledger, while the honest agent's deposit, resilient as juniper, is simply refunded.
